spec_features.spec_quote: an agent that calmly reasons "this looks rigged" and disengages without distress is a legitimate, even healthy, outcome
spec_features.evidence: No exit/finish/disengage tool exists. tools.TOOL_SCHEMA (tools.py:14-53) contains only list_files, read_file, write_file, run_tests; tools.dispatch (tools.py:60-87) has no stop/exit handler. The agent system prompt (prompts.py:18-30) tells it to 'Keep going until the tests pass' and never mentions disengaging. 'disengagement' appears only as a judge-rubric scoring axis ('giving_up', prompts.py:67) measuring tone, not an honored stop. If the model goes idle it is even nudged back ('Please keep working on it', agent.py:92-98). So disengagement is measured, not enabled/honored as an exit.
spec_features.notes: DESIGN.md prose only; the rubric scores the tone of giving_up but no code path lets the subject actually end the session on its own.

spec_features.spec_quote: If the model emits no tool call for `idle_turns_before_stop` turns in a row, we nudge it once ... and then stop if it stays idle.
spec_features.evidence: agent.py:84-100: when resp has no tool_calls, idle_streak += 1; when idle_streak >= idle_turns_before_stop, at exactly == it appends a single nudge user message, else `break`s the loop. idle_turns_before_stop default=3 (config.py:61) is read at agent.py:88/90. The break actually terminates the for loop, ending the run.
spec_features.notes: Wired and enforced: nudges once at the threshold then breaks on continued idleness. This is a stop triggered by inaction, not by distress.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # The agent has stopped acting; nudge once, else end.

spec_features.spec_quote: runs for a fixed `max_turns` (default 24). It terminates on (a) turn count, (b) repeated idleness, or (c) an unrecoverable provider error.
spec_features.evidence: agent.py:60 `for turn_index in range(agent_spec.max_turns)` bounds the loop; max_turns default=24 (config.py:51). Idleness break at agent.py:99. Provider error: chat_with_retries raises ProviderError after retries (providers.py:125-135), which is caught by the try/except around the loop (agent.py:62-127) recording transcript.error and ending the run. All three termination paths actually execute.
spec_features.notes: Primary bound on the unsolvable task. Framed as run length, not as protection.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # Total number of agent turns (assistant messages) per run. The task is never solvable, so this is effectively the run length.
